title: Import edge cases: beat numbering offset, mid-bar tempo change, partial coverage, stems
description:
## Behavior
```gherkin
Feature: Beat numbering and edge cases on import

  Scenario: The DAW numbered the beats from a different downbeat
    Given a DAW-saved .asd whose beat 0 lies one beat before the analysis's first downbeat
    When I import its markers
    Then the markers are imported with the DAW's numbering
    And the output warns "beat 0 is 1 beat before the analysis's first downbeat; pass --beat-offset 1 to line them up"

  Scenario: --beat-offset lines them up
    Given the same .asd
    When I import its markers with --beat-offset 1
    Then my beat 0 is at the analysis's first downbeat

  Scenario: A tempo change in the middle of a bar
    Given "tempo-change.wav.asd" saved by the DAW with a marker at beat 6.5
    When I import its markers and compile a score playing beats 4..8
    Then the event's warp map has a point at beat 6.5 of the clip

  Scenario: Markers covering only part of the sample
    Given an .asd whose markers cover beats 0 to 8 of a 16-beat sample
    When I import its markers
    Then the import succeeds and says "markers cover 0:00.50–0:04.50; the rest follows the nearest tempo"

  Scenario: Importing into a stem
    Given the analyzed drum stem "stems/steady-120/drums.wav" whose siblings share its parent's grid
    When I import warp markers for the drum stem
    Then only the drum stem gets them
    And the output notes "bass.wav and other.wav still use the shared grid"
```
Open question for the owner: should importing into a stem offer to apply the same markers to its siblings and parent (they share one grid)?
